subject.title: Memory dreaming run pegs the gateway event loop for ~10 min until killed; short-term recall store can never persist (2026.6.9, reproduces on unmodified dist)

question: Should maintainers require the reporter's v2026.6.9/v2026.6.11 process samples or a current-main large-store repro before queueing a fix for the dreaming event-loop peg?
rationale: The source has plausible hot paths, but the exact final-phase stall could be plugin-state replacement, candidate relocation, phase sweep work, or narrative/report handling; choosing the wrong repair could leave the outage intact.

options.title: Inspect samples first
options.body: Ask for or inspect the reporter's process samples and corpus shape, then queue the fix against the confirmed hot path.

options.title: Prototype bounded state writes
options.body: Start with the plausible SQLite/plugin-state replacement loop and require a large-store regression test before merge.

options.title: Fold into crash recovery
options.body: Defer this to interrupted-run lifecycle work, accepting that diagnostics may improve before the event-loop starvation is fixed.

recommendation.title: Inspect samples first
recommendation.body: Ask for or inspect the reporter's process samples and corpus shape, then queue the fix against the confirmed hot path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core storage and release history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding proof sufficiency.
